examples.en: I completely forgot what happened yesterday.
The thief took all the money.
The fields were totally ruined by the typhoon.
I forgot every single word I learned last night.
All of his lies were exposed.

examples.ko: 냉장고 안의 음식을 깡그리 먹어 치웠어요.
examples.en: I ate up all the food in the fridge.

explain: '모두', '전부'와 비슷하지만 하나도 남기지 않고 다 없어진다는 느낌이 강해요. '잊다', '없애다', '먹어 치우다'처럼 뒤에 오는 말과 잘 어울려요.

phrases.example: 시험이 끝나자마자 외운 내용을 깡그리 잊었어요.
phrases.en: As soon as the exam was over, I forgot everything I had memorized.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기억이 하나도 남지 않을 때 써요. '다 잊다'보다 완전히 사라진 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when no memory remains at all. It feels more complete than '다 잊다'.

phrases.en: My younger sibling ate up all the snacks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 하나도 남기지 않고 다 먹었다는 뜻이에요. '먹어 치우다'와 자주 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means eating every last bit of food. It pairs often with '먹어 치우다'.

phrases.en: I threw away all the documents in the drawer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉬운 비슷한 말이에요. '전부'는 중립적이고, '깡그리'는 하나도 남지 않았다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, similar word. '전부' is neutral, while '깡그리' implies nothing was left.

explain_en: Used with verbs of loss or removal: wiping out everything, forgetting it all without a trace. It is similar to '모두' and '전부', but it strongly suggests that nothing is left at all. It pairs well with verbs like '잊다', '없애다' and '먹어 치우다'.

t90.ax: The thief took all the money.

en: with a wriggle; with a twitch

examples.ko: 벌레가 손바닥 위에서 꿈틀 움직여서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A bug wriggled on my palm and I was startled.

examples.ko: 눈썹이 꿈틀 올라가는 걸 보니 화가 난 것 같아요.
examples.en: His eyebrow twitched upward, so he seems angry.
The sleeping baby's toes wriggled.
The fishing line twitched and a fish was caught.

examples.ko: 비 온 뒤에 지렁이가 꿈틀 기어 나왔어요.
examples.en: After the rain, an earthworm wriggled out.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣자 입꼬리가 꿈틀 올라갔어요.
examples.en: When he heard that, the corners of his mouth twitched up.

explain: 한 번 움직이는 느낌이에요. 계속 움직이면 '꿈틀꿈틀'이라고 해요. 벌레, 몸의 일부, 눈썹이나 입꼬리가 살짝 움직일 때 써요.

phrases.en: The earthworm is wriggling along the ground.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꿈틀'이 한 번이라면 '꿈틀꿈틀'은 계속 움직이는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '꿈틀' is a single movement, while '꿈틀꿈틀' is continuous wriggling.

phrases.en: The sleeping child's finger twitched.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꿈틀' 뒤에 '움직이다'를 붙이면 살짝 한 번 움직인 모습이 잘 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '움직이다' after '꿈틀' shows a single slight movement clearly.

phrases.en: I was startled and my shoulders twitched.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꿈틀'에 '하다'를 붙여 동사로 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form made by adding '하다' to '꿈틀'.

explain_en: A single slow squirming motion, like a worm. It describes a single movement. For continuous movement you say '꿈틀꿈틀'. It is used for bugs and for small body movements like eyebrows or the corners of the mouth.

examples.ko: 집에 있는 바퀴벌레를 완전히 박멸하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to completely wipe out the cockroaches in my house.
This product kills off mold.

examples.ko: 전문 업체가 우리 집 개미를 박멸했어요.
examples.en: A professional company exterminated the ants in our house.
To wipe out pests, you have to get rid of the eggs too.
It isn't easy to eradicate this disease.

examples.ko: 텃밭의 잡초를 박멸하는 방법 좀 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me how to wipe out the weeds in my garden plot.

explain: '없애다'보다 딱딱하고, 하나도 안 남기고 없앤다는 느낌이 강해요. 일상 대화에서는 '잡다, 없애다'가 더 자연스럽고, '박멸하다'는 광고나 뉴스에서 많이 보여요.

phrases.en: It is hard to completely eradicate mosquitoes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '완전히'와 함께 쓰면 뜻이 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 완전히 makes the meaning clearer.

phrases.en: That disease was eradicated long ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 없어지는 쪽에서 말하는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Passive form, viewed from what gets eliminated.

phrases.en: I got rid of all the bugs in my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: '박멸하다'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more natural in daily conversation.

explain_en: Strongest; killing insects or pests completely. It is stiffer than '없애다' and suggests leaving nothing behind. In daily talk '잡다' or '없애다' sounds more natural, while '박멸하다' shows up in ads and news.

examples.ko: 이 방에서는 음식물 반입을 일절 금지해요.
examples.en: Bringing food into this room is absolutely prohibited.

examples.ko: 그 일에 대해서는 일절 말하고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to say anything at all about that matter.

examples.ko: 회의 중에는 휴대폰을 일절 쓰지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't use your phone at all during the meeting.

examples.ko: 그는 단 음식은 일절 먹지 않아요.
examples.en: He never eats sweet food.

examples.ko: 약속 장소에 대한 연락이 일절 없었어요.
examples.en: There was no word at all about the meeting place.

examples.ko: 저는 그 계획에 일절 관여하지 않았어요.
examples.en: I had absolutely no involvement in that plan.

explain: '일절'은 뒤에 '않다, 없다, 금지하다'처럼 부정이나 금지 표현이 따라와요. 뜻은 '전혀'와 비슷하지만 안내문, 규칙, 공식적인 말에 더 잘 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '전혀', '아예'가 더 편해요.

phrases.example: 그 일에 대해서 제가 아는 것은 일절 없어요.
phrases.en: I know absolutely nothing about that matter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '없다'와 함께 써서 하나도 없다는 것을 강하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 없다 to say strongly that there is none at all.

phrases.en: I don't drink alcohol at all.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 행동을 아예 하지 않는다는 단호한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives a firm sense of not doing something at all.

phrases.en: I didn't know that story at all.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일절'과 뜻이 비슷하지만 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to 일절 but more comfortable in daily speech.

explain_en: '일절' is followed by a negative or prohibiting expression such as '않다', '없다' or '금지하다'. Its meaning is close to '전혀', but it suits notices, rules and formal speech better. In daily conversation '전혀' and '아예' feel easier.

examples.ko: 그 부대의 주둔은 삼 년 동안 계속됐어요.
examples.en: The unit's stationing there lasted three years.

examples.ko: 군인들의 주둔 때문에 마을이 조용하지 않아요.
examples.en: The village isn't quiet because of the soldiers stationed there.
The stationing period ended, so the unit came back.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 외국군의 주둔을 허락하지 않아요.
examples.en: This country does not allow foreign troops to be stationed here.
The soldiers' period of stationing is one year.
As the stationing dragged on, local residents also became uncomfortable.

explain: '주둔'은 뉴스나 역사 이야기에서 군대 이야기를 할 때 주로 나와요. 사람이 어느 곳에 잠깐 머무는 건 '머무르다'나 '묵다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: People who oppose the stationing of troops gathered.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주둔'과 가장 자주 같이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation with this noun.

phrases.en: The soldiers returned to their base.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대가 머무르는 장소를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the place where troops are stationed.

phrases.en: The stationed troops left the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어느 곳에 머무르는 군대 자체를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the troops that are stationed somewhere.

explain_en: 주둔 mostly shows up in news and history when talking about an army. For ordinary people staying somewhere for a while, Koreans say 머무르다 or 묵다.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 당뇨 가족력이 있어서 검사를 자주 받아요.
examples.en: Diabetes runs in my family, so I get tested often.
There was a box at the hospital to write down family medical history.
Even without a family history, you still need to take care of your health.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 암 가족력이 있는지 물어보셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor asked whether there is a family history of cancer.

examples.ko: 가족력이 있으면 일찍 검진을 받는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: If it runs in your family, it is good to get checked early.

examples.ko: 할아버지 때부터 고혈압 가족력이 이어져 왔어요.
examples.en: High blood pressure has run in our family since my grandfather's time.

explain: 병원 문진표에 자주 나오는 말로, 가족 중에 같은 병을 앓은 사람이 있는지를 말해요. '가족력이 있다/없다'로 쓰고, 병 이름을 앞에 붙여 '당뇨 가족력'처럼 말해요. 가족이 같은 병을 앓았다는 사실을 말할 뿐이어서 '유전'이라는 말과는 느낌이 달라요.

phrases.en: There is no family history of heart disease for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족 중에 같은 병을 앓은 사람이 없을 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when no family member has had the same illness.

phrases.example: 암 가족력이 있으면 검진을 일찍 받는 게 좋아요.
phrases.en: If you have a family history of cancer, it's better to get checkups early.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병 이름을 앞에 붙여 어떤 병의 가족력인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the disease name first to say which illness runs in the family.

phrases.en: The doctor asked about my family medical history.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 진료받을 때 자주 듣는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase you often hear at the hospital.

explain_en: It often appears on medical questionnaires and refers to whether family members have had the same illness. You say '가족력이 있다/없다' and put the illness first, as in '당뇨 가족력'. It only states that relatives had the illness, so it feels different from '유전' (heredity).

examples.ko: 할아버지는 오래된 만성병 때문에 약을 드세요.
examples.en: Grandfather takes medicine for a long-standing chronic disease.
For chronic diseases, steady management is the most important thing.

examples.ko: 당뇨나 고혈압 같은 만성병이 있으면 정기 검진을 받아야 해요.
examples.en: If you have a chronic disease like diabetes or high blood pressure, you need regular checkups.

examples.ko: 만성병을 가진 사람이 늘고 있다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news that the number of people with chronic diseases is rising.
My father has a chronic condition, so he is careful about his diet.

examples.ko: 만성병에는 생활 습관을 바꾸는 게 큰 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: For chronic diseases, changing your lifestyle helps a lot.

explain: 오래 낫지 않고 계속 관리해야 하는 병을 말해요. 뉴스나 병원에서는 '만성 질환'이라고도 하고, 반대로 갑자기 생겨 빨리 진행되는 병은 '급성'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 만성 질환이 있으면 정기 검진이 필요해요.
phrases.en: If you have a chronic illness, you need regular checkups.
phrases.nuance_ko: '만성병'과 같은 뜻으로, 병원이나 뉴스에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 만성병, used more in hospitals and news.

phrases.en: My father has a chronic disease.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 관리해야 하는 병이 있다는 사실을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone has a long-term condition.

phrases.en: I manage my chronic disease with exercise and diet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료보다 꾸준히 돌보는 것을 강조할 때 '관리하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '관리하다' emphasizes ongoing care rather than a cure.

explain_en: Medical term for long-lasting disease like diabetes or hypertension. It refers to an illness that doesn't go away and must be managed continuously. In the news or at hospitals it is also called '만성 질환', and an illness that comes suddenly and progresses quickly is called '급성'.

t90.ax: For chronic diseases, changing your lifestyle helps a lot.

examples.en: I got stung by a bee and my arm swelled up.
I got stung by a bee in the mountains and it really hurts.

examples.ko: 손등에 벌침이 박혀 있어서 빼 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: A stinger was stuck in the back of my hand, so I asked someone to pull it out.

examples.ko: 저는 벌침 알레르기가 있어서 늘 조심해요.
examples.en: I'm allergic to bee stings, so I'm always careful.

examples.ko: 벌침을 빼려면 카드로 살살 긁어 보세요.
examples.en: To remove the stinger, gently scrape it with a card.
My younger sibling went to the hospital because of a bee sting.

explain: 다쳤다고 말할 때는 '벌에 쏘이다'가 더 일상적이에요. '벌침'은 쏘는 침 자체나 그 상처를 말할 때 자연스러워요. '벌침에 쏘이다', '벌침을 빼다'처럼 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I got stung by a bee in the park and went to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: '벌에 쏘이다'가 더 일상적이지만, 침을 강조할 때 '벌침에 쏘이다'도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '벌에 쏘이다' is more everyday, but 벌침에 쏘이다 is also used when stressing the stinger.
phrases.en_equiv: to be stung by a bee

phrases.en: I carefully pulled out the stinger stuck in my skin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에 남은 침을 뽑는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for pulling out the stinger left in the body.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is allergic to bee stings, so he is careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 건강 이야기에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in medical and health talk.

explain_en: When you say you got hurt, '벌에 쏘이다' is the more everyday phrase. '벌침' sounds natural when you mean the stinger itself or the sting wound. It pairs with verbs like '벌침에 쏘이다' and '벌침을 빼다'.

examples.ko: 이 텀블러는 보온이 잘 돼서 겨울에 따뜻한 차를 넣어 다녀요.
examples.en: This tumbler keeps heat well, so I carry warm tea in it in winter.

examples.ko: 담요로 감싸면 음식을 오래 보온할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you wrap it in a blanket, you can keep the food warm for a long time.

examples.ko: 아기 방을 보온하려고 두꺼운 커튼을 달았어요.
examples.en: I hung thick curtains to keep the baby's room warm.

examples.ko: 이 외투는 보온해 주는 효과가 커요.
examples.en: This coat is very good at keeping you warm.
I kept the whole pot warm so the soup wouldn't get cold.
They say an air layer is important for keeping things warm.

explain: 차갑게 식은 것을 데우는 것이 아니라, 이미 있는 따뜻함이 빠져나가지 않게 지키는 것이에요. '보온병', '보온 도시락'처럼 명사로도 많이 쓰고, 반대로 시원함을 지키는 것은 '보냉'이라고 해요. '데우다'와 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: I brought warm water in a thermos.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜨거운 음료를 오래 따뜻하게 두는 병이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A bottle that keeps hot drinks warm for a long time.

phrases.example: 이 이불은 보온이 잘 돼서 겨울에 좋아요.
phrases.en: This blanket keeps heat well, so it's good for winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 따뜻함이 잘 유지된다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise how well something keeps warmth in.

phrases.en: I stuck plastic on the window to keep the room warm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 따뜻함을 지키려는 목적을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state the purpose of keeping heat in.

explain_en: It is not about heating something cold but about keeping existing warmth from escaping. As a noun it appears in '보온병' and '보온 도시락', and keeping something cool is '보냉'. Don't confuse it with '데우다' (to heat up).

examples.ko: 어머니가 꽃 모양 브로치를 선물해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mother gave me a flower-shaped brooch as a gift.
The mood changed after I pinned a brooch on my coat.
I inherited this brooch from my grandmother.
I don't know where my brooch fell off.

examples.ko: 옷깃에 작은 브로치 하나만 달아도 예뻐요.
examples.en: Even just one small brooch on the collar looks pretty.
The brooch pin is weak, so it keeps coming off.

explain: '브로치를 달다', '브로치를 꽂다'처럼 말해요. 목에 거는 목걸이나 손가락에 끼는 반지와는 함께 쓰는 동사가 달라요.

phrases.en: I pinned a brooch on my collar.
phrases.nuance_ko: '달다'와 같은 뜻이고, 핀으로 찌르듯 고정하는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same as 달다, with the feel of fixing it on with a pin.

phrases.en: I gave my friend a brooch for her birthday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 브로치를 선물로 줄 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the phrase for giving a brooch as a gift.
phrases.en_equiv: to give a brooch as a gift

phrases.en: That brooch is really pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 브로치를 칭찬할 때 조사 '가'와 함께 쓰는 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a sentence for praising a brooch, using the particle 가.

explain_en: You say '브로치를 달다' or '브로치를 꽂다'. The verbs differ from those used with a necklace (worn around the neck) or a ring (put on a finger).

examples.en: On Lunar New Year, the children wore colorful jeogori and bowed to their elders.
That striped-sleeve jeogori is really lovely.
The saekdong jeogori is usually worn by young children.
At the first-birthday party, I saw a baby dressed in a saekdong jeogori.
I picked a skirt that goes well with the saekdong jeogori.
It's a blanket as colorful as a saekdong jeogori.

explain: 소매에 여러 색 줄무늬를 댄 한복 저고리예요. 보통 명절이나 돌에 아이들이 입는 옷으로 떠올려요. '저고리'는 한복의 윗옷을 말해요.

phrases.en: The baby wore a saekdong jeogori at the first birthday party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 입을 때는 '입다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '입다' (to wear) for clothing.

phrases.example: 색동저고리에 분홍 치마를 입은 아이가 인사했어요.
phrases.en: A child in a saekdong jeogori and a pink skirt said hello.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저고리와 같이 입는 아래옷인 '치마'를 같이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Mention the skirt, the bottom worn together with the jeogori.

phrases.en: The saekdong jeogori is so lovely.
phrases.nuance_ko: '곱다'는 색이나 모양이 부드럽고 예쁠 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: '곱다' fits when colors or shapes look soft and pretty.

explain_en: It is a hanbok jacket with multicolored stripes on the sleeves. People usually picture it as clothing children wear on holidays or first birthdays. '저고리' is the upper garment of a hanbok.

examples.en: I apply foundation thinly on my face.
This foundation sticks well to the skin.
The foundation shade is too dark for me.

examples.ko: 새 파운데이션을 사려고 화장품 가게에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the cosmetics shop to buy a new foundation.
I ran out of foundation.
I asked my friend to recommend a foundation.

explain: 피부색을 고르게 하는 화장품이고, 가게에서는 '쿠션'이나 '비비크림'과 같이 비교해서 골라요. 색은 '21호', '23호'처럼 호수로 말해요.

phrases.en: I use foundation shade 21.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색은 호수로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shades are named by number.

phrases.en: I picked a foundation that suits my skin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서 살 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often used when shopping.

phrases.en: It's summer, so I changed my foundation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절이나 피부에 따라 다른 제품으로 쓸 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when switching products by season or skin condition.

explain_en: Loanword for skin makeup applied as a base. It is a makeup product for evening out skin tone, and in shops people compare it with 쿠션 and 비비크림. Shades are given by number, like '21호' and '23호'.

examples.en: This region is counted as a key battleground in the election.

examples.ko: 역사책에 나온 유명한 격전지를 찾아가 봤어요.
examples.en: I visited a famous battle site mentioned in history books.
That island was a fiercely fought battleground long ago.
A memorial hall stands at the battle site now.
The candidates go from one battleground district to another campaigning.
The scenery of the old battleground is very peaceful now.

explain: 원래는 치열한 전투가 벌어진 곳이고, 선거 뉴스에서는 누가 이길지 알기 어려운 지역을 '격전지'라고 해요. '선거 격전지'가 자주 쓰이는 말이에요.

phrases.en: The biggest battleground of this election is Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: '최대'를 붙여 가장 경쟁이 센 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '최대' marks the place with the toughest competition.

phrases.example: 그 도시는 전쟁 때 격전지가 됐어요.
phrases.en: That city became a battlefield during the war.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치열한 싸움이 일어난 곳이 되었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the place became the site of fierce fighting.

phrases.en: A monument stands at the old battlefield.
phrases.nuance_ko: 역사 이야기에서 지난 전투 장소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a past battle site in history talk.

explain_en: Originally it means a place where fierce fighting took place, and in election news it also refers to a district where the winner is hard to predict. '선거 격전지' is a common phrase.

examples.ko: 추석 전날 귀성길에 올랐다가 열두 시간 만에 고향에 도착했어요.
examples.en: I set off for my hometown the day before Chuseok and arrived twelve hours later.

examples.ko: 귀성길에는 휴게소마다 사람이 가득해서 화장실 가기도 힘들어요.
examples.en: On the way to your hometown, every rest stop is packed, so even going to the restroom is hard.

examples.ko: 올해는 귀성 대신 영상 통화로 인사드렸어요.
examples.en: This year I greeted them by video call instead of going home.

examples.ko: 귀성객이 몰려서 고속버스 표가 모두 매진됐어요.
examples.en: Holiday travelers crowded in, so all the express bus tickets sold out.
I ordered a gift set for the trip home in advance.
I checked the traffic on the way to hometowns on the news.

explain: 명절에 고향으로 내려가는 일을 말해요. '귀성길', '귀성객', '귀성 인파'처럼 뉴스에 자주 나오고, 반대로 서울로 돌아오는 것은 '귀경'이에요.

phrases.en: I set out for my hometown on the morning before Seollal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명절에 고향으로 출발한다는 뜻의 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation for setting out for one's hometown on a holiday.
phrases.en_equiv: to set out for one's hometown

phrases.example: 귀성객을 위해 임시 열차를 더 운행해요.
phrases.en: They are running extra trains for people traveling to their hometowns.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명절에 고향에 가는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: People traveling to their hometowns during a holiday.

phrases.en: A crowd of hometown-bound travelers filled the terminal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 많이 몰린 모습을 뉴스처럼 표현해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news-style phrase for a large crowd of travelers.

explain_en: Visiting hometown at Chuseok or Seollal, with traffic jams. It refers to going down to your hometown for a holiday. It appears in the news in phrases like '귀성길', '귀성객' and '귀성 인파', and the opposite, coming back to Seoul, is '귀경'.
